newsitem.title: USA: WinStar sees smaller losses, capital outlay.
newsitem.headline: WinStar sees smaller losses, capital outlay.

text.p: WinStar Communications Inc said Tuesday that it expects its capital expenditures to be lower than originally expected over the next three years by about $50 million.

It also said that the rate of growth in its quarterly EBITDA losses, or losses before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization, is expected to slow after the second quarter and peak by the end of the year, with declining EBITDA losses expected in 1998.
Interest expense for the company totaled $31 million in the first half of 1997.

The company said it had planned to spend $500 million on capital expenditures in the three year period covering 1997, 1998, and 1999. It now expects to spend less than $450 million, due mainly to lower expenditures on customer premises equipment than in its original budget.
The company said it ended the second quarter with $343 million in cash and a $150 million credit facility, for total funds potentially available of almost $500 million.
This capital, said WinStar, combined with readily available lease financing, if desired, is expected to fund its capital expenditures and the company's expected 1997 and 1998 EBITDA losses.

WinStar is a national local communications company, serving business customers, long distance carriers, fiber-based competitive access providers, mobile communications companies and local telephone companies.
